memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "In all cases of illegal possession of an ox, a donkey, a sheep, a garment, or any other lost property about which somebody says, 'This is mine,' both parties are to bring their cases before the judges. The one whom the judges declare guilty must pay back double to the other." - Exodus 22:9 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
When two people both claim, "This is mine," how is the truth found? God's law provides a way: bring the dispute before appointed judges, let the matter be examined, and let justice be done. God did not leave His people to settle every quarrel by whoever shouted loudest or hit hardest. He built pathways for truth to come to light and for fairness to prevail.

This tells us something important: God cares about justice being actually done, not just talked about. He established structures so that the wronged could be vindicated and the guilty held accountable. Behind every honest human court stands God's own passion for what is right. He is the God who loves justice (Ps 37:28).

Yet human judges are limited. They can only weigh the evidence before them; hidden truths escape them. This is why it is such a comfort that above every earthly court sits a perfect Judge who sees all things and cannot be deceived. If you have ever been falsely accused or wrongly treated, take heart — nothing is hidden from God. He will bring every hidden thing to light (1 Cor 4:5). We can entrust our case to Him, the Judge who always gets it right.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
Do I trust God as the final Judge when human justice falls short?
Am I quick to defend truth and fairness for others who are wronged?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, You are the perfect Judge who sees all things. When I am wronged or misjudged, help me entrust my case to You, confident that You will bring truth to light. Amen.
